Input_or_Condition: The customer request is too vague or ambiguous to determine the intended support task reliably.
The customer intent is clear but the requested topic is outside the supported MVP scope.
Resolving an identified customer intent requires a business action that the AI is not allowed to perform autonomously.
An approved policy required for a reliable answer cannot be retrieved or does not provide the rule required to resolve the request.
Approved policy sources contain materially conflicting rules required to resolve the request and no approved precedence rule resolves the conflict.
Operational order data is required but the Order Management System cannot be accessed or the required lookup fails.
Information required to continue can reasonably be provided by the customer but is missing or ambiguous.
A required internal field or business fact is missing null or unusable in an otherwise available approved source.
The customer provides an order identifier but no matching order can be found in the Order Management System.
The customer request contains two or more distinct intents that map to different supported use cases or require different processing paths.
The requested order is uniquely identified and current order-status information is available in the Order Management System.
The customer reports a delivery delay but the expected delivery date has not yet passed.
The expected delivery date has passed but the shipment remains within the waiting or grace period defined by Shipping Policy.
The delivery delay has reached the Shipping Policy condition requiring investigation or escalation.
The Order Management System shows the parcel as delivered but the customer reports that it was not received.
The identified order and item satisfy the applicable standard return conditions defined by Returns Policy.
The identified order or item clearly fails one or more applicable standard return conditions defined by Returns Policy.
The standard Returns Policy does not allow the return and the customer requests an exception requiring a discretionary decision.
The customer asks how to return an item and the applicable procedure does not require information about a specific order or item.
The correct return procedure depends on information about a specific order item or product category.
The relevant order is identifiable and the available operational facts allow standard refund eligibility to be evaluated using Refund Policy.
Standard Refund Policy does not resolve the request and the customer asks for an exception requiring a discretionary decision.
The customer asks a general informational question covered by Shipping, Returns, or Refund Policy and no order-specific decision or business action is required.
